Hi Priya / Jordan,

Thanks again for the time today — really appreciate the clear signals on what success looks like for the Acme evaluation. As promised, attached is a draft competitive bake-off test plan and a short Redwood vs hyperscaler matrix. The plan is intentionally prescriptive so we can run apples-to-apples tests across the vendors you mentioned (AWS Bedrock endpoint you have access to, GCP Vertex AI, and our Hosted API / Dedicated infra).

High-level proposed tests (we included details in the spreadsheet):
- Latency: p50/p95 for 256-token prompts and 1024-token prompts (target p95 < 250ms for 256 tokens, stretch p95 < 400ms for 1024 tokens)
- Throughput: sustained QPS bursts (50 req/s and 200 req/s) with and without batching enabled
- Cost: tokens-per-dollar comparison normalized to your workload (we'll run identical prompt/response mixes)
- Quality/regression: top-1 answer agreement on your 50 eval prompts and BLEU/ROUGE for structured outputs
- Failure modes: cold-start latency, kv-cache behavior for chat flows, and graceful degradation with fallback model variants

Owners / asks:
- Redwood owner: Marissa Cole (SE) — will own test harness, end-to-end scripts, and produce the results sheet.
- Acme owner: Priya Sharma — will provide the final eval prompt set and representative sample traffic shape.
- Timeline: kickoff tests next Wed (2026-03-18), results snapshot by Fri (2026-03-20), debrief Mon (2026-03-23).

Please review the attached plan and matrix and call out any gaps or additional hyperscaler configurations we should include (e.g., instance types, quantization settings). If the timeline looks good, we'll lock in owners and I will share the test harness repo + creds for the Redwood Dedicated test pool.

Attachments: acme-bakeoff-test-plan.xlsx, acme_requirements.pdf, redwood-vs-hyperscaler-matrix.pdf

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,

- For hyperscaler comparisons please include:
  * AWS Bedrock (we'll provide the Bedrock account + endpoint; please test both 1) default managed infra and 2) provisioned throughput option if available)

Thanks Priya — adding schema validation and hallucination checks to the plan. Quick internal notes / owner assignments so everyone is aligned:

- Test harness & infra provisioning (Redwood Dedicated + Hosted + hyperscaler accounts): Priyom Das (SE) — will provision the Dedicated pool, create temporary keys for the Bedrock and Vertex runs (we'll use short-lived creds), and share per-run infra metadata in the results sheet.
- End-to-end runner and metrics (latency, p50/p95, qps): Marissa Cole (SE) — will provide the scripts and CloudWatch/Stackdriver query templates for the hyperscalers and the Redwood tracing dashboard hooks.
- Quality eval automation (top-1 agreement, hallucination detection, JSON schema validation): Marissa + Priyom — Marissa will add the schema validation harness; Priyom will add automated hallucination heuristics (n-gram overlap + entity-check against Acme canonical dataset).
- Cost calc & normalization: Vanessa Ortiz — collect SKU/instance details and compute tokens-per-dollar normalized to Acme workload.
- Customer coordination & signoff: Vanessa + Aditya Rao (manager) — lead debrief and commercial next steps.

Success criteria (proposed gating):
1) Quality: >= 90% schema-valid outputs AND hallucination rate <= 5% on the 50 eval prompts.
2) Latency: p95 <= 250ms for 256-token prompts; p95 <= 400ms for 1024-token prompts (under typical traffic shape).
3) Cost: total normalized tokens-per-dollar within 1.25x of Acme's current hyperscaler baseline for the same prompt mix.
4) Reliability: no more than 1% error rate and graceful fallbacks for cold-starts during the 24h stress window.

I'll start populating the test plan spreadsheet with the exact commands we will execute and sample outputs. Priya — once you upload the eval prompts and traces we can load them into the harness.
